notes: The check uses a dynamically linked non-PIE C fixture compiled with -O0 -fno-builtin. It verifies eight distinct library calls, real arguments/results, output artifacts and target exit records for statuses 0 and 7.
The target exit status is read from its trace record; the ltrace process return code is recorded separately and must not be silently interpreted as target success.
Function prototypes determine argument decoding. The normal APT configuration is /etc/ltrace.conf; use -F for explicit prototype files/directories.
Inlining, static linking, missing PLT calls, unusual ABI or optimized/PIE binaries can reduce the calls visible to this old locked release. The qualification scope is explicitly recorded.
Kernel ptrace restrictions may block tracing even when --version succeeds. The check does not modify ptrace policy or attach to unrelated processes.
The upstream version probe and the exact Debian package identity are separate checks. A privately extracted Debian package is not an APT install/remove transaction.

The host-sensitive capability check records denied ptrace as blocked. The separate functional check performs the complete trace assertions on a capable host; neither check measures physical hardware performance.
usage.summary: Trace dynamically linked program library calls and decoded arguments using ltrace prototype libraries; investigate runtime calls in compiler-produced binaries.
